Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Inventory Part window opens.

Step 2:

  • Description holds the text.

Step 3:

  • Part Number reads number 1.

Step 4:

  • The manufacturer shows in the Manufacturer field.

Step 5:

  • The category shows in the Category field.

Step 6:

  • Cost reads $10.00.

Step 7:

  • The window closes and the part is saved.

Step 8:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 9:

  • Exactly one entry has number 1, and it now shows the manufacturer you picked: an entry pointing to a manufacturer that no longer exists counts as having none.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S7-R6d: “A linked entry has a manufacturer only when it points to a manufacturer that exists in this organization. An entry that points to none takes the one picked in the dialog.”
  • S7-R6b: “A linked entry with no manufacturer takes the one picked in the dialog. An entry that already has a manufacturer keeps it.”
  • Story 7, context note: “Context note (S7-R6d): many existing entries point to a manufacturer that no longer exists. The data cleanup in SV-10033 runs before this feature is released. Manufacturers cannot be deleted in ShopView, so an entry pointing to a missing manufacturer comes only from data saved before the release.”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026
